title: Sri Lanka batting flops ahead of Pakistan Test series | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 6 November 2026 00:20
-     - 22

ISLAMABAD: Sri Lanka’s batting once again flopped in their second innings of the 3-day warm-up match against a PCB Patron’s XI played at the Islamabad Cricket Club Oval here yesterday.

Apart from the two half-centuries scored by skipper Kusal Mendis and opener Lahiru Udara in the first innings, Sri Lanka’s top order failed to deliver and they had to recover from a shaky afternoon session of 51-4 at tea to build an overall lead of 193 by the close.   

Sri Lanka closed the second day at 121-6 thanks to a 56-run sixth wicket stand between Anjala Bandara (34) and Milan Rathnayaka (27*).

Sri Lanka’s top order was rattled by the pace of Shoaib Akhtar Jnr who dismissed Lahiru Udara for 15 and Dinesh Chandimal for his second duck of the match, in his opening spell and later came back to break the partnership between Bandara and Rathnayaka by having Bandara caught behind to end the day with 3/22 off 9 overs.

Pasindu Sooriyabandara tried out in his new position as opener, made only 14 to follow his first innings score of 8. Kusal Mendis was run out for 3 and Sonal Dinusha was out hit wicket for 22.

Resuming the day from overnight 43-2, the Patron’s XI fought back but were limited to 151-8 before declaring. Opening batter Azan Awais was the lone standout, scoring a solid half-century (50 off 85 balls, 9 fours).

Sri Lanka’s fast bowlers Lahiru Kumara, Dilshan Madushanka and Rathnayaka bowled tight lengths to pick up two wickets apiece.

The match will head into its third and final day today as Sri Lanka looks to extend their lead before setting a target for the Patron’s XI.

This red-ball fixture serves as the final tune-up for the touring Sri Lankan side before they head to Rawalpindi for the first official Test match beginning on 9 November.

Scores:

Sri Lanka 223-7 decl. and 121-6 at close (Sonal Dinusha 22, Anjala Bandara 34, Milan Rathnayaka 27*, Shoaib Akhtar Jnr 3/22) leads PCB Patron’s XI 151-8 decl. (Azan Awais 50, Mohammad Taha 29, Tayyab Arif 30, Lahiru Kumara 2/16, Dilshan Madushanka 2/32, Milan Rathnayaka 2/24) by 193 runs.

title: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 6 November 2026 00:06
-     - 13

Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo said he is retiring from international football. The 41-year-old forward has scored 146 goals and won 234 caps for his country - both world records - since making his debut in 2003.

He walked out of the Portugal camp in September after being told he would not start the Nations League match against Denmark, resulting in a £215 fine and a 30-day suspension.

“To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team,” Ronaldo said in an Instagram video. “I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world. Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone - they are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.”

Portugal will today announce their squad for this month’s Nations League fixtures - against Denmark at home and Wales away. The PFF said it will not “let this farewell take place without due tribute”.

A statement read: “It is our firm and immense desire to organise, plan, participate and actively collaborate in what will always be a fitting tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo’s immense career, in which fans and the country can applaud and celebrate, once again, the player who has given us so much.”

Ronaldo played in six European Championships. Portugal were runners-up in 2004 and champions in 2016, but did not progress beyond the semi-finals of the World Cup during his career. Portugal captain since 2008, he won the inaugural Nations League in 2019 and in 2025. Ronaldo’s great rival and Argentina legend Lionel Messi retired from international football on an emotional night in front of an 85,000-strong crowd in Buenos Aires in October.

SAFF Football Tournament – 15th Edition

India defeated traditional rival Pakistan 3-2 in the curtain raiser of the 15th edition of the SAFF Football Tournament played at the National Stadium, Dhaka, Bangladesh yesterday.

Team India dominated proceedings from the outset, while Pakistan made some valiant efforts only at the latter stages of the game, which was too little too late, as India snatched a sensational victory.

title: Sri Lanka kick-start U19 Asia Cup with facile win | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 6 November 2026 00:04
-     - 22

Right-arm medium-fast bowling all-rounder Kaushika Kumarasinghe ripped through the Malaysian batting line-up for 88 taking 5/30 off 6 overs to give Sri Lanka a winning start to their Asian Cricket Council (ACC) Under19 Asia Cup campaign at Al Amerat, Oman yesterday.

Invited to bat first Oman were bowled out in 28.1 overs with Kumarasinghe, a former first eleven captain of Kandy St Anthony’s College, running through the opposition, keeping things simple and straight to bundle them out for a paltry total.

Only one batsman entered double figures – opener Syamil Aqil who hit 51 off 50 balls (7 fours, 2 sixes) before falling to leg-spinner Vigneshwaran Akash who finished with figures of 3/7 off 4.1 overs.

Despite losing skipper Viran Chamuditha for a third ball duck, Sri Lanka had no problems reaching their target of 89. Rehan Peiris, Royal College, Colombo’s prolific run-scorer hit a flawless 54* off 45 balls (7 fours, 1 six) and shared an unbroken second wicket stand of 91 off 81 balls with Senuja Wekunagoda (30* off 35 balls, 4 fours) to see Sri Lanka home by nine wickets with plenty to spare.

Sri Lanka plays Bangladesh who lost to Afghanistan by 113 runs yesterday in their next Group B match on Saturday.

Scores: 

Malaysia (U19) 88 (28.1) (Syamil Akli 51, Kaushika Kumarasinghe 5/30, Vigneshwaran Akash 3/7) are defeated by Sri Lanka (U19) 91-1 (13.5) (Rehan Peiris 54*, Senuja Wekunagoda 30*)
